transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… my doctor sort of pushed me to come. She says I’ve gotten too thin. I guess I can see it too, like my work pants are hanging loose on me now, and I keep having to pull them up when I’m cleaning the halls. Funny thing is those pants used to feel snug after the holidays, you know, when everybody brings cookies to the break room.

But… I don’t know. When the number on the scale is lower, part of me feels relieved. Even if people are saying it’s not good.
Have you been eating less than usual or avoiding certain foods because you’re worried about gaining weight?

I mean… yes, I suppose I have been eating less. I still cook proper plates for my husband and my mother-in-law, you know, meat and potatoes or whatever we’ve got, because they need a real dinner. My mother-in-law is very particular about how things are cooked, too, so that takes some doing.

But then by the time I sit down, I’ll think… well, coffee is fine for me, or just a few vegetables. Sometimes half a piece of toast. It feels like enough, or I tell myself it is. And if I’m honest, part of it is because I don’t want to start putting weight back on.
Do you find yourself feeling very anxious or fearful about gaining weight, or do you feel like you need to keep your weight as low as possible even if others are concerned about your weight loss?

Yes… I do get scared about it. Like if I eat something heavier, biscuits or pasta or something like that, then the rest of the day I’m thinking it’s going to show on me somehow. I’ll keep checking myself, like my waist or how my clothes sit.

It sounds silly when I say it. My husband likes pasta, so I’ve made it plenty of times, and my mother-in-law always says it needs more salt—she says that about everything—but if I actually eat a real serving, I start thinking I need to make up for it somehow. Like I have to keep things low, even if other people are telling me I’m already too thin.
After eating, do you ever make yourself sick, take laxatives, or exercise more than you should to try to control your weight or keep from gaining weight?

Um… I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t make myself sick or anything like that. Laxatives—no, not really, unless… well, my mother-in-law used to keep all sorts of things in the medicine cabinet, you know, she saves everything, even cough syrup from years ago, which I keep telling her is not safe.

But no, I’m not doing that to lose weight. And exercise… I’m on my feet a lot at work already, walking the halls and emptying bins, so I don’t really go out and do extra on purpose. I might fuss around the house after dinner, but that’s just dishes and laundry and whatnot.
Do you feel like your weight or shape has a big impact on how you see yourself, or do you worry that you might be perceiving yourself differently than others do?

Yes… I suppose it does. I don’t like admitting that, because it sounds vain, and I’ve never thought of myself as a vain person. I wear the same sort of clothes most days anyway, work trousers, cardigan, nothing fancy.

But when I feel small and neat, like everything is tucked in and controlled, I feel like I’m managing properly. Like I’ve got myself in hand. And then if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even a little full… even if it’s just after eating or my skirt’s sitting wrong, I feel awful. Like I’ve let myself go.

I know other people might not see what I’m seeing. My husband will say I look fine, or that I’m too thin, but I don’t always believe it. I get stuck on what I see.
Have you had any medical conditions or changes in your health recently that might explain your weight loss?

I don’t… I’m not sure, really. I can’t think of some illness or anything that would explain it, if that’s what you mean.

I mean, I’ve had the usual little aches and bits that come with getting older, and at work there’s always something—my knees complain if I’m doing stairs all day, especially when they’ve left boxes in the hallway again, which they’re not supposed to—but nothing new that I’d point to and say, “That’s why.”

No doctor has told me there’s some medical reason. At least, not that I know of.
Have you ever had episodes where you feel like you've lost control over how much you're eating, or do you ever eat a lot in a short period of time and then feel bad about it?

I don’t know… I wouldn’t say I eat a lot in one go. Not like a whole big spread or anything. I’m usually the opposite, really—well, I mean, I try to be careful.

Sometimes if I have more than I meant to, like if someone brings biscuits into the break room—there’s always someone doing that, and then they leave crumbs everywhere and I end up cleaning it anyway—I might feel cross with myself after. But I don’t think it’s like losing control. I’m not sure what would count as “a lot,” though.
Do your worries about your weight or shape ever interfere with your daily life, like making it hard to focus on work, interact with others, or enjoy activities you used to like?

It does, yes… though I still go to my cleaning shifts. I mean, I do the work. Floors still need doing whether I’m fussing about myself or not, and if I don’t do it properly someone notices—well, sometimes they don’t, actually, but I notice.

But other things… I’ve stopped going along properly to family dinners, and the church meals too. I’ll say I’m busy, or I’ll help clear plates instead, because then I’m sort of there but not really sitting down with everyone. My husband says I’m around people without joining in, which hurt to hear, but… I suppose he’s not wrong.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, like missing periods or them stopping altogether?

Oh… I’m not sure that’s something I can really answer in the usual way now. I haven’t been keeping track of anything like that—well, not for a long time. At my age it’s not really been… you know, something that happens anymore.

I remember when I did used to have to think about it, always making sure I had things in my bag, especially at work because you can’t just leave in the middle of mopping a hallway. But lately, no, I haven’t noticed any change like that.
Have you ever been diagnosed with a medical condition that could explain your weight loss, such as a thyroid problem or gastrointestinal issue?

I don’t think so… no one’s told me I have something like that. I mean, I’ve seen doctors for ordinary bits and pieces over the years, like everyone does, but I can’t remember anyone saying, “This is why your weight’s changed,” or anything clear like that.

I did wonder once if maybe it was just getting older, because everything changes when you get older—my knees certainly remind me of that after a long shift—but no, I don’t think there’s been a diagnosis like the ones you’re asking about.
Have you ever gone without enough food because of a lack of money or other resources?

No, I don’t think so… not in the way you mean. We’ve had tight weeks, of course. Everyone has, haven’t they? Especially when bills come at the wrong time, or the car needs something, and then you’re standing in the shop thinking, well, I don’t need the nice bread this week.

But I wouldn’t say there wasn’t food because we couldn’t get it. My husband’s always been careful about keeping basics in, and I’m the sort who can make things stretch—my mother was like that too, never wasted a thing. So… no, I don’t think lack of money is why I’ve gone without.
Do you feel like your weight or shape is something you judge yourself on, even if other people don't seem to notice the same things you do?

Yes… I suppose I do, though I don’t always think of it like “judging,” exactly.

It’s more that when I’m small and neat-looking, I feel like I’m keeping myself together, if that makes sense. Like the house is in order. I used to be very particular about cupboards being wiped down properly at work—people don’t notice unless it’s wrong, you know—and I suppose I’m a bit like that with myself too.

But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks even a little bit full, I get this horrible feeling like I’ve let myself go. Even if no one else says anything. I know other people probably aren’t looking that closely, but I notice it.
Do you find that your sense of self-worth is strongly related to how you feel about your body shape or weight?

Yes… I think it is, more than I like to admit.

When I stay small and neat, I feel like I’m handling everything properly, like I’ve got myself under control. It’s silly, because I used to say the same sort of thing about keeping the floors done right at work—if the corners were clean, I felt I’d done a decent job, even if nobody else noticed.

But with my body, if I catch my stomach looking even the least bit full in the mirror, I feel awful, like I’ve let myself go somehow. Like I’ve failed at keeping myself together. So yes, I suppose how I feel about myself gets tied up in that.
